newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore share index loses ground, rally likely.
newsitem.headline: Singapore share index loses ground, rally likely.

text.p: Singapore's benchmark stock index ended lower on Wednesday, partially cancelling out an upward blip caused by heavy buying of a few selected component shares late on Tuesday.
But the broader market was a little firmer and several dealers predicted a firmer trend for the rest of the week.
"Fund demand is beginning to perk up and most institutions are still underweight for the region," said one dealer. "I shouldn't be surprised if we ended the week a bit higher."
The Straits Times Industrials share index ended 11.65 points lower at 2,064.36. The all-share index was up 0.76 at 498.64.
Top of the volume was Malaysia's Public Bank foreign, which fell 21 cents to Singapore $2.32 on news foreigners could buy local shares, thus eroding the premium for the foreign tranche.
In Kuala Lumpur, Public Bank's local share tranche was up 24 sen at 3.56 ringgit.

Shares in property group DBS Land ended two cents up at S$4.86 after hitting a high of S$4.98 midday following news it had purchased 19.16 percent of healthcare and property group Parkway Holdings on Tuesday. Parkway was up 15 cents at S$6.60.
